answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake per identity: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, like a velvet rope admitting one guest at a time. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand deposits, and proven misbehavior forfeits the stake, so the attack price scales linearly while honest agents get their money back. New identities enter through a narrow inlet with probationary quotas and rate-limited rewards, graduating to full earning only after a history of honest attestations, the way a mesa rises in tiers. Faking identity stays possible but no longer free.
